thread:
elaine: Pushed the model-routing v2 rollout to canary (us-east). Starting quick smoke pass now — looking for latency regressions, error spikes, and any functional breakage. @raj @sasha can you watch metrics for the next 10m? deploy-bot should have the canary summary up.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy finished on 3 hosts. healthchecks: PASS. canary_id=cr-2015006789, duration=45s.

raj: On it. running a quick health curl and a small synthetic load:
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -sS -w "\\nCODE:%{http_code} TIME:%{time_total}" -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.test/v1/route/health || true; done
```

raj: Quick numbers from the last 5m window: p50 ~22ms, p95 ~85ms, errors ~0.02%. no obvious error spikes in the canary group.

sasha: Traces look clean — no tail latencies on KV cache misses. sampling shows same model variant is serving. I checked the token-serving QPS and it's within expected.

mike: Ran the smoke convo set (20 prompts) against canary, all responses coherent and no timeout errors. left one minor formatting mismatch in tool-calling response (open question but not a blocker).

jen: Code review for the roll flag is green, infra toggles applied. If we need to abort, plan is rollback to routing v1 and lift canary.

elaine: Thanks team. Rollback criteria we agreed on: sustained errors >0.2% OR p95 latency >400ms for 5 consecutive minutes OR functional failures on the canary smoke suite. If any of those happen, react with :arrow_backward: and I'll trigger the rollback command. Quick rollback command (if needed):
```
# rollback to previous routing variant
rcli deploy set-routing --env us-east --variant v1 --reason "canary rollback"
```

raj: putting a short watch on dashboards, will post if anything trends.

sasha: Keeping an eye on traces for 30m, will escalate to eng-oncall if I see anomalies.

elaine: Excellent. If nothing odd in 20m we'll start expanding to 10% traffic. tagging this thread for post-rollout notes. :thumbsup:

mike: noted — will follow up with the small formatting fix PR and a quick verif once it's merged.

jen: Congrats on smooth canary. Will update deploy doc with the minor tweak.

elaine: Closing the loop here — current verdict: canary healthy, no rollback. continuing gradual ramp. thanks everyone.
